The Columbian Exchange Transforms the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Every disease in the Exchange moved in only one direction, from west to east.
options.misconception: Smallpox, measles, and influenza moved west; the directions were mixed, not one-way.

options.text: The origin of syphilis is still debated, so historians qualify claims about it.
Syphilis proves that the Exchange harmed Europe as much as the Americas.
options.misconception: One debated disease does not balance the epidemics that devastated the Americas.

options.text: Historians have settled that no disease ever crossed from the Americas to Europe.
options.misconception: The origin of syphilis is still debated; nothing here is settled.

rationales.general:
1. Name the debate. Some historians trace syphilis to the Americas; others say it was already in Europe.
2. Ask what is missing. The evidence does not settle the origin, so no side can claim certainty.
3. Check the scale. One debated disease does not balance the westbound epidemics.
4. Rule out the rest. Diseases moved both ways in principle, but the dying went one way.
Remember: when historians disagree about an origin, say what is debated, not what is settled.
rationales.B: The origin of syphilis is still debated, so historians qualify their claims about it rather than stating one side as fact.
rationales.A: Smallpox, measles, and influenza moved west. The directions were mixed, not one-way.
rationales.C: One debated disease does not balance the epidemics that devastated the Americas.
rationales.D: The origin of syphilis is still debated. Nothing here is settled.

stem: Some historians say syphilis sailed east from the Americas to Europe, while others say it was already in Europe before 1492. What does this disagreement best show about the Columbian Exchange?

stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, stating the argument the questions evaluate.
stimulus.text: A historian argues that the Columbian Exchange was an exchange of goods between the Eastern and Western Hemispheres that spread prosperity to people on both sides of the Atlantic.
